ledger.claim: POL-NS-04 limb (a) is satisfied on the face of the chat log. At 12:41:05, roughly six and a half minutes before the driver terminated the trip, the rider sent 'hi im at the entrance 3 phv pickup point, which car ah?' — a message that both states the rider's own pickup point and asks the driver for his position. That is a locating-or-coordinating message sent inside the waiting window, and it was delivered at 12:41:06.

POL-NS-04 limb (b) is satisfied twice over. The chat log holds three messages — two from the rider and one system message — and not a single message from the driver at any point, so there is no reply within the 120 seconds following the 12:41:05 message (nor following the 12:44:40 message). Separately, trip_record.in_app_calls is empty: the driver never placed an in-app voice call before terminating the trip. The clause is written as 'neither … nor', and the driver made neither attempt.

POL-NS-04 limb (c) is satisfied on the full rider track. The trace carries an unbroken rider_presence record of 105 fixes, all 105 qualifying, with a maximum distance from the pickup pin of 39.93 m and a mean of 21.08 m, and a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph — a stationary device sitting inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider_presence_radius_m. That is the rider inside the presence radius for every qualifying fix across the window, not merely the majority. The narrative filed with the claim refers to Entrance 1, while the contemporaneous chat message and trip_record both record Entrance 3; the point does not disturb the analysis, because limb (c) is a distance test and the rider's device never left a 40 m radius of the pin.

With all three limbs of POL-NS-04 made out, the consequence is fixed by the clause itself: 'the rider is exonerated and the cancellation fee refunded in full, with no driver compensation payable'. No driver compensation is owed on this record, and the rider asks for FULL_REFUND of the contested amount under POL-GEN-03, which defines FULL_REFUND as the whole contested amount returned to the filing party.

The driver cannot save the fee through POL-NS-01. His dwell arithmetic is not in issue — the trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 340 seconds from 12:41:50 to 12:47:30, which meets the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum — but POL-NS-01 charges the fee only 'where all four conditions hold and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them', and POL-NS-04 is one of those displacing clauses. The fee is therefore not chargeable under POL-NS-01 however well the dwell is made out.

The cancellation reason code RIDER_UNREACHABLE is not borne out by the record. The rider's first message was read at 12:41:22 and the second at 12:44:52 — seventeen and twelve seconds after being sent — so the driver saw both. The driver made no in-app call at all, and answered neither message, while parked inside the 120 m arrival radius of that same pin. A driver who genuinely could not reach the rider had a call button and a reply box and used neither; POL-NS-01 limb (d) may be satisfied by the code the driver selected, but the conduct behind the code is a coordination failure on the driver's side, which is exactly what POL-NS-04 exists to answer.

This is not a wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity case, so the driver cannot route the fee through POL-NS-03. The driver's own trace carries 35 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, and his nearest approach to the pin was 94.94 m — within the radius, not in the 120-to-400 m band POL-NS-03 governs. The rider's track was within 40 m of the same pin throughout. Both devices were at the pickup point; the failure was the driver's silence, not a mismatch of location, and no POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill arises.

The amount to be returned is the disputed cancellation-fee line and nothing else. The fare breakdown itemises cancellation_fee 4.00 against a LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of 4.00, shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the dispute contests 4.00. The platform fee of 0.50 is not contested and is not sought. FULL_REFUND therefore moves SGD 4.00 back to the rider.

No escalation trigger is engaged on this record, so the case is decidable now rather than being held. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not fire, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so POL-NS-09(d) does not fire. Every artifact the rider relies on — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issues recorded, so POL-NS-08 and POL-NS-09(e) are not engaged either.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are made out on this record, so the baseline cancellation fee is chargeable. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:41:50. (b) The 100%-coverage GPS trace places the driver inside the pickup geofence from that same timestamp. (c) He then held position for a continuous in-geofence dwell of 340 seconds, 40 seconds beyond the 300-second minimum for this zone class. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 12:47:30 under reason code RIDER_UNREACHABLE, after the dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded.

The arrival geofence test in POL-NS-02 is met on the wider radius this zone class allows: pickup_zone_class is LARGE_VENUE, so the arrival radius is 120 m rather than 50 m, and the driver's own track records a closest approach of 94.94 m to the pin with 35 consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes spanning the dwell.

There is no waiting-period shortfall, and therefore no premature cancellation under POL-NS-06: the measured in-geofence dwell is 340 seconds against the LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 seconds, a surplus of 40 seconds, so the refund route built on a shortfall is not engaged and cannot refund this fee.

The arrival marker is genuine, so the false-arrival route in POL-NS-05 does not open: at the 12:41:50 arrival timestamp the driver was already inside the arrival radius and not more than 300 m from the pin, and he is stationary at 0.0 km/h throughout the in-geofence dwell, so he was not in motion on an expressway or arterial road when the marker was set.

This is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03: that clause reaches only a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius, and the trace places this driver inside the 120 m radius, at a closest approach of 94.94 m, for the whole dwell.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard does not trip on this driver, so compensation is not withheld on that ground and the case does not escalate under POL-NS-09(d): the guard requires BOTH no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a rate above 0.08, and the recorded trailing-30-day figure is 3, so the first limb fails.

Where the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, namely SGD 3.20, with the residual 20 percent retained as platform service fee; that is exactly the figure the payments ledger already computes, and it is the amount the ruling should carry as driver_compensation_sgd.

The fee line is arithmetically sound and carries no integrity defect: fee_schedule.resolution_rule takes the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), and fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee records exactly SGD 4.00, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

The bundle the driver relies on is clean at weight 1.0 — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown each carry admissibility status COMPLETE with no issue codes, the trace has zero gaps and 100 percent coverage, and the chat log holds all three messages its own count records — so there is no POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment and POL-GEN-02 caps nothing here.

The rider's account of where she stood is internally inconsistent and should be weighed accordingly: her dispute claim says she was standing at the Entrance 1 PHV pickup point the whole time, while the only message she sent identifying her position, at 12:41:05, reads 'entrance 3 phv pickup point', which is also the entrance named in trip_record.pickup.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand on this record, and it is refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's arrival and dwell are not the problem. The trip record shows an 'arrived' event at 12:41:50 (limb (a)), the GPS trace places the driver 94.94 m from the pin — inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius — from that same timestamp (limb (b)), he then held position for a continuous 340-second in-geofence dwell, 40 seconds over the 300-second minimum (limb (c)), and the trip was terminated by the driver at 12:47:30 under RIDER_UNREACHABLE with no boarding event (limb (d)). So POL-NS-01 is made out on its four limbs. But POL-NS-01 charges the fee only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-04 does.

POL-NS-04 is satisfied on all three limbs. (a) The 12:41:05 message, 'hi im at the entrance 3 phv pickup point, which car ah?', both states the rider's own position and entrance and asks for the driver's; the 12:44:40 message, 'boss? i still cannot see u leh', is a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. Both are locating/coordinating messages sent inside the waiting window. (b) The chat log contains no driver message at any point — the middle entry is the platform's own 'Your driver has arrived' system notice, not a reply — and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made an in-app call before terminating. (c) The rider track's 105 fixes, all qualifying, sit within a maximum of 39.93 m of the pin (mean 21.08 m), well inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius, for every fix rather than merely the majority. The clause therefore applies, and its own words fix the result: the rider is exonerated, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

On the driver's claims: POL-NS-01 is made out but displaced by POL-NS-04, so it does not carry the fee. The SGD 3.20 compensation under POL-NS-07 does not arise, because compensation is payable only where POL-NS-01 stands and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. POL-NS-02 (geofence met), POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance band not reached — the driver never fell in the 120–400 m band), POL-NS-05 (marker genuine, driver stationary) and POL-NS-06 (no shortfall) are each correctly analysed, and each simply confirms the fee is decided by POL-NS-04 rather than by them. The anti-farming guard under POL-NS-07 does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the 4 required, and 3/142 = 0.021, below 0.08), so no escalation follows from it. The fee line is arithmetically sound — the greater of the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X tier fee — so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. The 'Entrance 1' reference in the rider's filed narrative against 'Entrance 3' in the contemporaneous chat message and trip record is immaterial: limb (c) is a distance test, and the rider's device stayed within 40 m of the pin throughout.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: both counterparty dispute counters are 0, rider no-show disputes in 30 days is 0, the sole-evidence limb is not engaged, and confidence is well above the 0.70 floor. No clause produces a referral, so referrals is empty. The refund moves only the contested cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00; the SGD 0.50 platform fee is not contested and is not touched. Confidence is capped at 1.0 — the deciding facts rest on the trip record, GPS trace and chat log, each at weight_multiplier 1.0 — and I set it at 0.92.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
